summary: A rule defines what "correct" looks like; an audit is what checks it — so this comes first. We'll open the rule library and start one called "Google Analytics fires on every page". You set the conditions, since only you know which tags and values count as right.

parameters.ruleSubject: Google Analytics fires on every page
parameters.ruleName: Google Analytics fires on every page

steps.say: Open Tag & Variable Rules in the sidebar, under Standards. If the sidebar is collapsed to icons, widen it first.

targetFallback.description: the "Tag & Variable Rules" link under Standards in the left sidebar

steps.say: Naming it "Google Analytics fires on every page".

targetFallback.description: the rule name field at the top of the builder

action.value: Google Analytics fires on every page

steps.say: Pick the tag and the condition that make this rule pass, then continue.

targetFallback.description: the Next button in the rule builder

steps.say: Save it. It's now attachable to any audit under Standards.

targetFallback.description: the Save button in the rule builder
